elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: M&I must “defend Customer,” and the supplied definition of Customer expressly includes its Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: M&I must indemnify Customer, which includes Affiliates, and Section 14.2(B) expressly covers claims by third parties.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Coverage is limited to claims that Services or M&I software infringe a United States patent, copyright, or trademark; it does not cover Deliverables generally or all intellectual-property rights.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: The indemnity covers only violations of laws or regulations protecting persons or protected classes, not M&I's breach of applicable law generally.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No data-breach indemnity trigger appears in the rendered language.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: The clause has no unqualified indemnity trigger for M&I's gross negligence or wilful misconduct; its acts-or-omissions provision is limited to specified property damage or Customer financial loss.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 requires the indemnitee to give notice of a covered third-party claim.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 entitles the indemnifying party to assume control of the defence with reasonably satisfactory counsel.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 requires the indemnitee to cooperate fully and assist in all reasonable respects.

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Customer's indemnity additionally covers inaccurate representations, discrimination or harassment, workplace injury or death, property damage, financial loss, and Section 6.6(B) matters.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: M&I indemnifies Customer against third-party claims that Services or M&I software infringe United States patents, copyrights, or trademarks.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-modification exclusion is included; the permitted exclusion is not invoked, leaving broader IP coverage.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: No Customer-combination exclusion is included; the permitted exclusion is not invoked, leaving broader IP coverage.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-specification exclusion is included; the permitted exclusion is not invoked, leaving broader IP coverage.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3(C) requires M&I to procure continued use or modify or replace the affected Services or software so it is non-infringing.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: If none of those remedies is available, M&I must refund fees paid for the affected Services or software.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: Section 13.4 caps M&I's Section 14.2(B) indemnification liability at three times the annual fees paid by Customer.
